samples.rationale: Grouping and sorting live in an immutable record (`SpecialtyDirectory.of`, List.copyOf in both compact constructors), so `VetController.showSpecialtyDirectory` only binds, delegates, and names a view — no new business rule in the controller, and the unit is testable without framework context. Deduction: `SpecialtyRepository` applies the Repository pattern to `Specialty`, a lookup value and not an aggregate root, with no ADR; its `ORDER BY specialty.name` duplicates `BY_SPECIALTY_NAME`, putting ordering in two places. Tests are behavior-named, four-phase, whole-object compared, and use a hand-written `SpecialtyRepository` lambda instead of a mock framework; `NO_HOLDERS_MARKUP = "none"` couples to rendered markup, and the stable-order test bundles two concerns. PRD REQ-VET-003, contracts rows, invariants note, open questions, and all eleven bundles move together.

Grouping logic sits in an immutable record (`SpecialtyDirectory.of`, defensive `List.copyOf`) rather than the controller, so the new rule is unit-testable without the framework — the pyramid argument the principles ask for. Debt: a specialty HTTP surface is bolted onto `VetController` instead of a `SpecialtyController` prefixed by its own domain noun, and ordering is specified twice (`ORDER BY specialty.name` in `findSpecialties()` plus `BY_SPECIALTY_NAME` in the record), so a future change can diverge silently. `Comparator.comparing(Vet::getId)` assumes non-null ids. Unit tests are exemplary (behavior names, factories, whole-object `isEqualTo`); the web test asserts literal markup `"none"` and the template's `#{none}` key is never added to any bundle the patch touches. Docs move everywhere: PRD requirement, open questions, contracts, scale table, eleven locales.

Grouping and ordering live in the immutable `SpecialtyDirectory` record (`of()`, defensive `List.copyOf`), so `VetController.showSpecialtyDirectory` only binds, delegates and selects a view — no new controller rule. `SpecialtyRepository` is read-only, matching the out-of-scope decision. The one structural quibble: the specialty surface is bolted onto `VetController`, though the naming rule prefixes a controller by the surface it serves. Tests are behavior-named, factory-built, whole-object compared (`isEqualTo(directoryOf(...))`), and cover empty holders and stable order; but `NO_HOLDERS_MARKUP = "none"` asserts rendered markup, `#{none}` is used without a bundle key added alongside `specialty`, and `aSpecialty`/id constants are duplicated across both test classes. PRD REQ-VET-003, contracts rows, invariants and a Scale/Load section all move; nothing visible is left stale.
